entities.summary: The IRR Southern Line, also known as the Baghdad–Basra Railway Line, is a railway line between the Iraqi capital of Baghdad and the port city of Basra in Iraq. The line is roughly 550 kilometres (340 mi) long, with intermediate stops including Karbala, Musayyib, Diwaniya, Samawah, Nasiriya and Um Qasr. A proposal was put forward to convert the railway route to high-speed rail and connect the city of Najaf, but the plan was never realised. Next to the commuter train to Falluja, it is one of the two only routes in Iraq that service passengers.
